passages.text: This is the word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel: Hear this, O elders; and give ear, all who dwell in the land. Has anything like this ever happened in your days or in the days of your fathers?
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Joel.
Joel is the son of Pethuel.
This is the word of the LORD that came to Joel.
Elders, listen to this message.
All who live in the land, pay attention.
Has anything like this happened in your days?
Has anything like this happened in the days of your fathers?
passages.original: דְּבַר־ יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֔ה אֶל־ יוֹאֵ֖ל בֶּן־ פְּתוּאֵֽל׃ שִׁמְעוּ־ זֹאת֙ הַזְּקֵנִ֔ים וְהַֽאֲזִ֔ינוּ כֹּ֖ל יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ הֶהָ֤יְתָה זֹּאת֙ בִּֽימֵיכֶ֔ם וְאִ֖ם בִּימֵ֥י אֲבֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Tell it to your children; let your children tell it to their children, and their children to the next generation.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Joel, son of Pethuel.
God gave Joel a message for the people.
God said, “Tell this message to your children.
Your children must tell it to their children.
Their children must tell it to the next generation.”
passages.original: עָלֶ֖יהָ לִבְנֵיכֶ֣ם סַפֵּ֑רוּ וּבְנֵיכֶם֙ לִבְנֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם לְד֥וֹר אַחֵֽר׃

passages.text: What the devouring locust has left, the swarming locust has eaten; what the swarming locust has left, the young locust has eaten; and what the young locust has left, the destroying locust has eaten.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Joel, son of Pethuel.
God described a great disaster.
Locusts came to the land.
The first locusts devoured the crops.
What the first locusts left, the swarming locusts ate.
What the swarming locusts left, the young locusts ate.
What the young locusts left, the destroying locusts ate.
Nothing remained after the locusts finished.
passages.original: יֶ֤תֶר הַגָּזָם֙ אָכַ֣ל הָֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה וְיֶ֥תֶר הָאַרְבֶּ֖ה אָכַ֣ל הַיָּ֑לֶק וְיֶ֣תֶר הַיֶּ֔לֶק אָכַ֖ל הֶחָסִֽיל׃

passages.text: Wake up, you drunkards, and weep; wail, all you drinkers of wine, because of the sweet wine, for it has been cut off from your mouth.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
He addresses those who drink too much wine.
He calls them drunkards.
He tells them to wake up.
He tells them to weep.
He speaks to everyone who drinks wine.
He tells all wine drinkers to wail.
He says the sweet wine is gone.
He says the sweet wine has been taken away from them.
They cannot drink it anymore.
passages.original: הָקִ֤יצוּ שִׁכּוֹרִים֙ וּבְכ֔וּ וְהֵילִ֖לוּ כָּל־ שֹׁ֣תֵי יָ֑יִן עַל־ עָסִ֕יס כִּ֥י נִכְרַ֖ת מִפִּיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: For a nation has invaded My land, powerful and without number; its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and its fangs are the fangs of a lioness.
passages.sermon:
A nation has invaded My land.
This nation is powerful.
No one can count its people.
Its teeth are like the teeth of a lion.
Its fangs are like the fangs of a lioness.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ גוֹי֙ עָלָ֣ה עַל־ אַרְצִ֔י עָצ֖וּם וְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֑ר שִׁנָּיו֙ שִׁנֵּ֣י אַרְיֵ֔ה וּֽמְתַלְּע֥וֹת לָבִ֖יא לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: It has laid waste My grapevine and splintered My fig tree. It has stripped off the bark and thrown it away; the branches have turned white.
passages.sermon:
A powerful nation invaded God's land.
This nation destroyed God's grapevine.
This nation broke God's fig tree.
It stripped off the bark from the trees.
It threw the bark away.
The branches turned white.
passages.original: שָׂ֤ם גַּפְנִי֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה וּתְאֵנָתִ֖י לִקְצָפָ֑ה חָשֹׂ֤ף חֲשָׂפָהּ֙ וְהִשְׁלִ֔יךְ הִלְבִּ֖ינוּ שָׂרִיגֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Wail like a virgin dressed in sackcloth, grieving for the husband of her youth.
passages.sermon:
A young woman has lost her husband.
She is a virgin.
She wears sackcloth.
She mourns deeply.
She grieves for her husband from her youth.
You must wail like this woman.
passages.original: אֱלִ֕י כִּבְתוּלָ֥ה חֲגֻֽרַת־ שַׂ֖ק עַל־ בַּ֥עַל נְעוּרֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Grain and drink offerings have been cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests are in mourning, those who minister before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The house of the LORD has lost its grain offerings.
The house of the LORD has lost its drink offerings.
The priests serve the LORD.
The priests mourn.
passages.original: הָכְרַ֥ת מִנְחָ֛ה וָנֶ֖סֶךְ מִבֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אָֽבְלוּ֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים מְשָׁרְתֵ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: The field is ruined; the land mourns. For the grain is destroyed, the new wine is dried up, and the oil fails.
passages.sermon:
The field is ruined.
The land mourns.
The grain is destroyed.
The new wine is dried up.
The oil fails.
passages.original: שֻׁדַּ֣ד שָׂדֶ֔ה אָבְלָ֖ה אֲדָמָ֑ה כִּ֚י שֻׁדַּ֣ד דָּגָ֔ן הוֹבִ֥ישׁ תִּיר֖וֹשׁ אֻמְלַ֥ל יִצְהָֽר׃

passages.text: Be dismayed, O farmers, wail, O vinedressers, over the wheat and barley, because the harvest of the field has perished.
passages.sermon:
Farmers, you feel dismay.
Vinedressers, you wail.
You mourn for the wheat.
You mourn for the barley.
The harvest of the field has perished.
passages.original: הֹבִ֣ישׁוּ אִכָּרִ֗ים הֵילִ֙ילוּ֙ כֹּֽרְמִ֔ים עַל־ חִטָּ֖ה וְעַל־ שְׂעֹרָ֑ה כִּ֥י אָבַ֖ד קְצִ֥יר שָׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: The grapevine is dried up, and the fig tree is withered; the pomegranate, palm, and apple— all the trees of the orchard—are withered. Surely the joy of mankind has dried up.
passages.sermon:
The grapevine is dried up.
The fig tree is withered.
The pomegranate tree is withered.
The palm tree is withered.
The apple tree is withered.
All the trees of the field are dried up.
The joy of mankind has dried up.
passages.original: הַגֶּ֣פֶן הוֹבִ֔ישָׁה וְהַתְּאֵנָ֖ה אֻמְלָ֑לָה רִמּ֞וֹן גַּם־ תָּמָ֣ר וְתַפּ֗וּחַ כָּל־ עֲצֵ֤י הַשָּׂדֶה֙ יָבֵ֔שׁוּ כִּֽי־ הֹבִ֥ישׁ שָׂשׂ֖וֹן מִן־ בְּנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Put on sackcloth and lament, O priests; wail, O ministers of the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, O ministers of my God, because the grain and drink offerings are withheld from the house of your God.
passages.sermon:
Priests, put on sackcloth.
Priests, mourn.
Ministers of the altar, wail.
Ministers of my God, come.
Spend the night in sackcloth.
The house of your God has no grain offerings.
The house of your God has no drink offerings.
God has withheld these offerings.
passages.original: חִגְר֨וּ וְסִפְד֜וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים הֵילִ֙ילוּ֙ מְשָׁרְתֵ֣י מִזְבֵּ֔חַ בֹּ֚אוּ לִ֣ינוּ בַשַּׂקִּ֔ים מְשָׁרְתֵ֖י אֱלֹהָ֑י כִּ֥י נִמְנַ֛ע מִבֵּ֥ית אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם מִנְחָ֥ה וָנָֽסֶךְ׃

passages.text: Consecrate a fast; proclaim a solemn assembly! Gather the elders and all the residents of the land to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God commands the people to act.
He tells them to set apart a time for fasting.
He tells them to announce a special gathering.
He tells them to bring together the elders.
He tells them to gather all the people who live in the land.
He tells them to come to the house of the LORD their God.
He tells them to cry out to the LORD.
passages.original: קַדְּשׁוּ־ צוֹם֙ קִרְא֣וּ עֲצָרָ֔ה אִסְפ֣וּ זְקֵנִ֗ים כֹּ֚ל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ בֵּ֖ית יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם וְזַעֲק֖וּ אֶל־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Alas for the day! For the Day of the LORD is near, and it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Joel speaks to the people of Israel.
He warns them about a coming day.
This day is called the Day of the LORD.
The Day of the LORD is very near.
This day will bring great trouble.
Destruction will come from the Almighty God.
People will feel sorrow and fear on that day.
passages.original: אֲהָ֖הּ לַיּ֑וֹם כִּ֤י קָרוֹב֙ י֣וֹם יְהוָ֔ה וּכְשֹׁ֖ד מִשַׁדַּ֥י יָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: Has not the food been cut off before our very eyes— joy and gladness from the house of our God?
passages.sermon:
Food is gone.
We see this with our own eyes.
Joy is gone from the house of our God.
Gladness is gone from the house of our God.
passages.original: הֲל֛וֹא נֶ֥גֶד עֵינֵ֖ינוּ אֹ֣כֶל נִכְרָ֑ת מִבֵּ֥ית אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ שִׂמְחָ֥ה וָגִֽיל׃

passages.text: The seeds lie shriveled beneath the clods; the storehouses are in ruins; the granaries are broken down, for the grain has withered away.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Joel speaks about a time of great disaster from God.
The seeds lie shriveled under the soil.
The storehouses stand empty.
The granaries are broken down.
The grain has withered away.
passages.original: עָבְשׁ֣וּ פְרֻד֗וֹת תַּ֚חַת מֶגְרְפֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם נָשַׁ֙מּוּ֙ אֹֽצָר֔וֹת נֶהֶרְס֖וּ מַמְּגֻר֑וֹת כִּ֥י הֹבִ֖ישׁ דָּגָֽן׃

passages.text: How the cattle groan! The herds wander in confusion because they have no pasture. Even the flocks of sheep are suffering.
passages.sermon:
The cattle groan.
The herds of cattle wander in confusion.
They have no pasture.
The flocks of sheep also suffer.
passages.original: מַה־ נֶּאֶנְחָ֣ה בְהֵמָ֗ה נָבֹ֙כוּ֙ עֶדְרֵ֣י בָקָ֔ר כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין מִרְעֶ֖ה לָהֶ֑ם גַּם־ עֶדְרֵ֥י הַצֹּ֖אן נֶאְשָֽׁמוּ׃

passages.text: To You, O LORD, I call, for fire has consumed the open pastures and flames have scorched all the trees of the field.
passages.sermon: I call to You, O LORD.\r\nFire has consumed the open pastures.\r\nFlames have scorched all the trees of the field.
passages.original: אֵלֶ֥יךָ יְהוָ֖ה אֶקְרָ֑א כִּ֣י אֵ֗שׁ אָֽכְלָה֙ נְא֣וֹת מִדְבָּ֔ר וְלֶ֣הָבָ֔ה לִהֲטָ֖ה כָּל־ עֲצֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: Even the beasts of the field pant for You, for the streams of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the open pastures.
passages.sermon:
The wild animals suffer.
They long for You, Lord.
The streams have dried up.
Fire has burned the open fields.
passages.original: גַּם־ בַּהֲמ֥וֹת שָׂדֶ֖ה תַּעֲר֣וֹג אֵלֶ֑יךָ כִּ֤י יָֽבְשׁוּ֙ אֲפִ֣יקֵי מָ֔יִם וְאֵ֕שׁ אָכְלָ֖ה נְא֥וֹת הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃פ
